thread:
alex: Heads-up: we're scheduling a maintenance window to consolidate a few small GPU pools and rebalance spot-backed nodes in us-west1. Window: 2025-10-03 02:00-06:00 UTC. Goal: reduce fragmentation, reclaim spot capacity, and apply kernel + NVIDIA driver updates. Expect ~15% temporary capacity reduction in us-west1 during backfill, up to ~3h of active work.
maria: timeline looks ok from SRE side. which pools exactly? any dedicated/reserved customers affected?
alex: target pools: gpu-small-1, gpu-small-2, gpu-small-3 and spot-cohort-Theta. No dedicated/reserved pools are in scope unless someone pinned to those exact nodes (we checked manifests). Plan is canary in eu-west1 -> rack-cohort rolling in us-west1 by physical rack. Action: cordon -> drain -> update -> uncordon.
sam: what's the expected impact on serving? more 5xx or just higher tails/latency?
alex: shouldn't see 5xx. likely higher tails and some queued requests while backfill runs. fallback policy will route overflow to quantized model variants; autoscaler thresholds will be bumped slightly to give headroom. If errors spike we abort.
lee: ops checklist? backfill strategy? cache warm procedures?
alex: checklist (short):
1) Canary in eu-west1 for 20m against read-only endpoints.
2) Mark cohort nodes cordoned: `kubectl cordon <node>`
3) Drain: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300`
4) Apply kernel + driver update, run smoke tests.
5) Run `scripts/warm_kv_prefix.sh --prefix=model_512 --rate=100r/s` to warm KV cache before bringing node back.
6) Backfill from dedicated pools if needed with `tools/backfill --from=dedicated --to=spot --target=10`
7) Uncordon and monitor dashboards for 30m.
maria: canary should be against `redwood-7b-v2` and `redwood-3b-quant` read-only traffic. abort criteria: error rate > 0.5% or latency > baseline + 200ms.
ops-bot: scheduled_maintenance: window_enqueued by alex for 2025-10-03T02:00:00Z -> 2025-10-03T06:00:00Z
deploy-bot: rolling_job_created: infra/pool-consolidation/us-west1 starts 2025-10-03T02:00:00Z
oncall: I'll take paging for the window. please publish live status updates and link the runbook in #incidents.
alex: runbook: https://internal/runbooks/pool-consolidation-2025 (contains rollback steps: `kubectl uncordon`, capacity spillback policy, and a playbook to restore spot autoscaling).
finance: quick ask: what's the expected cost impact? rough number for exec summary?
alex: rough estimate: reclaim ~12 GPUs of spot capacity across the cohort, ~USD 18k/mo in spot savings at current rates. we'll produce a formal calc post-run with exact reclaimed GPU-hours and effective unit cost change.
maria: reminder: update cross-region routing policy in case us-west1 latency degrades. ops-sre please validate GSLB priority weights before window.
alex: noted — will update GSLB weights and post before canary.
sam: can we temporarily add autoscaler buffer? +2 nodes in affected ASGs for 4 hours would reduce churn.
alex: yes: setting `min_replicas += 2` for affected groups for window.
lee: prefer `--grace-period=300` on drain to avoid evicting long RPCs. also include `--pod-selector='!stateful'` for stateful jobs.
alex: done — will include both flags in the drain step.
oncall: if anything needs an immediate rollback, ping me and tag @oncall with the shortcode "rollback".
maria: scheduled notice: please post to #general and #partners 24h before, and send an enterprise notice to customers that may see higher latency.
alex: will do final confirmation 24h prior and again 2h prior. tagging @oncall @ops-bot. any other blockers?
maria: none from SRE. :thumbsup:
alex: thanks all — posting this to the ops calendar and the maintenance tracker now. will share runbook edits and the final resource savings calc after the run.
